children: Fujifilm will invest Rs 800 crore in phases to establish a semiconductor materials plant in Dholera, supporting Tata Electronics’ Rs 91,000-crore fab and efforts to localise critical chipmaking supplies

Japanese technology company Fujifilm will invest approximately Rs 800 crore to establish a semiconductor materials manufacturing plant in Gujarat’s Dholera Special Investment Region (DSIR) as part of a strategic partnership with Tata Electronics.

The companies signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on Thursday to develop a semiconductor materials ecosystem around Tata Electronics’ upcoming 300 mm fabrication facility in Dholera. The investment will be made in phases, with the plant intended to ensure the availability and movement of materials required by the fab.

The agreement comes as India seeks to build capabilities across the semiconductor value chain, including materials, chemicals, equipment, fabrication and advanced packaging. Tata Electronics has been announcing a series of partnerships at Semicon India 2026 covering several of these areas.

Under the Fujifilm agreement, the two companies will work on localising critical raw materials used in semiconductor fabrication and help Indian chemical manufacturers develop the capability to produce high-purity chemicals. Fujifilm will provide technology, quality assurance and manufacturing process know-how as part of the collaboration.

Fujifilm's semiconductor materials business covers products used across multiple stages of chip manufacturing, while the company has manufacturing operations across Japan, the United States, Europe and Asia.

"Tata Electronics is committed to building a resilient, world-class semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem in India," Randhir Thakur, CEO and managing director of Tata Electronics, said in a statement.
The partnership, he added, would strengthen the materials supply chain for the Dholera fab, while supporting the development of a semiconductor ecosystem in India.

Fujifilm Holdings CEO Teiichi Goto said the company views India's expanding semiconductor market as an opportunity for growth in its semiconductor materials business. He said Fujifilm's range of materials covering front-end and back-end manufacturing could contribute to the development of India's semiconductor industry.

Tata Electronics is developing the Dholera fab with an investment of Rs 91,000 crore, or about USD 11 billion. The facility will manufacture chips on 28nm to 110nm technology nodes and is designed to serve sectors including automotive, consumer electronics, computing and data storage, wireless communications and artificial intelligence.

The planned fab is expected to have a monthly capacity of 50,000 wafers for analog and logic integrated circuits, according to Tata Electronics. The company is developing the facility in partnership with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC).

The Fujifilm investment is therefore aimed at establishing part of the supporting industrial base alongside the fab, reducing reliance on imported materials and creating local manufacturing capabilities for semiconductor-grade chemicals.

The announcement also adds to a wider set of partnerships Tata Electronics unveiled around Semicon India 2026. The company has separately entered into an agreement with Dutch chipmaker Nexperia covering wafer fabrication and assembly and testing, while other partnerships announced this week span advanced packaging, indigenisation and talent development.
